title_original: La Contemporaine, Nanterre : Didier Lefèvre, the images that tell

blocks.text: On the occasion of the entry of his complete archive into La Contemporaine and of the bicentennial of photography , the exhibition and publication dedicated to photojournalist Didier Lefèvre (1957–2007) look back at the singular career of the hero of the celebrated graphic novel The Photographer (Emmanuel Guibert, Didier Lefèvre, Frédéric Lemercier, published by Dupuis from 2003 to 2006, translated into eighteen languages). A biologist and pharmacist by training, Didier Lefèvre traveled the world on humanitarian missions: in Afghanistan alongside Doctors Without Borders, as well as in Malawi, Cambodia and Kosovo. His work is inseparable from his attachment to writing, through which he expressed his doubts and reflections about his profession. He bore witness to the technical upheaval of the shift from film to digital and to the economic constraints weighing on reporters.

Besides humanitarian photography, Didier Lefèvre captured French society and its faces at the turn of the century: politics, notably the rise of the National Front; the fight against AIDS; European agricultural policies; the business world, through commissioned portraits of company executives. He also returned regularly to certain favorite subjects: bullfighting, the Paris-Roubaix race and firefighters. The Didier Lefèvre archive adds to La Contemporaine’s photojournalism collections, in continuity with the archives of Élie Kagan and Thérèse Bonney. Through more than three hundred previously unpublished photographs and documents (contact sheets, posters, personal notebooks), the exhibition and its accompanying catalog reveal a remarkable collection of images that tell stories.

“Didier [Lefèvre] was a press photographer who didn’t work like a press photographer,” observes Florence Aubenas , journalist and author, who often accompanied him on assignments for the daily Libération. “He was a storyteller as much as a photographer: funny, honest and never showy.”

With contributions from Florence Aubenas, journalist and author; Alain Bujak, photographer and comic-book writer; Eleanor Davey, historian of humanitarianism and author; Gilles Dorronsoro, professor of political science; Juliette Fournot, former MSF head of mission in Afghanistan; Emmanuel Guibert, comic-book author and writer; Alain Keler, photographer; Bernard Le Bars, firefighter and photographer; Frédéric Saumade, professor of social anthropology; Alain Tendero, photographer. Edited by Clara Bouveresse (photography historian, associate professor at Université d’Évry-Paris Saclay) and Coline Silvestre (head of photographic collections at La Contemporaine), curators of the exhibition. 256-page catalog, priced at €29.50
Didier Lefèvre, les images qui content from November 18, 2026 to May 15, 2027 La Contemporaine – Nanterre 184 Cours Nicole Dreyfus 92000 Nanterre, France www.lacontemporaine.fr
